signature_moves: Daybreak-spectrum dome icon: 'Dia' = day; a sunrise (blue dawn -> warm horizon) as a translucent glass lozenge — name, concept and colour resolve into one mark
One mark, two renders: the cover's white logo glyph is the exact silhouette of the icon's coloured dome
Serif-display wordmark paired on a contrast axis with a plain grotesque tagline — editorial warmth, deliberately unlike a dev-tool
Dread-relief emotional framing: a screaming-portrait photograph sells the problem so the product is the relief (brand storytelling, not a product shot)

aesthetic.direction: Luxury/editorial-cinematic (design-craft 'Luxury/fashion' x 'Editorial/literary'): high-contrast serif wordmark + grotesque tagline, near-black drenched ground, full-bleed emotional photography — BRAND direction, not a UI aesthetic
aesthetic.cluster_hint: editorial-dark-brand (marketing lockup; NOT a UI style cluster)

psychology: Von Restorff — a single white lockup on a black field is the one salient thing; total figure/ground isolation (brand lockup, not a UI CTA)
Aesthetic-usability / processing fluency — an extremely spare, polished brand card raises the trust prior before any product is seen (Lindgaard 50ms; Reber & Schwarz)
Loss / emotional framing — the tagline names the status quo as 'dread' and the photo dramatises it, so the product reads as relief (Kahneman-Tversky loss framing, used in copy+image, not UI)
Jakob's Law — cannot be assessed: browser-convention conformance needs the actual chrome, which is absent
